new.s: Which programmes were merged to form the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana in 1989?
new.x: JRY (1989) merged the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) and the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) into one wage-employment scheme.

new.s:
Arrange the following programmes in chronological order of their launch:
1. SGSY
2. IRDP
3. JRY
4. DAY-NRLM
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: IRDP came in 1978-80, JRY in 1989, SGSY in 1999 and DAY-NRLM in 2011.

new.s: Which expert group included both food and non-food needs such as housing, clothing, education, health and transport in its poverty line?
new.x: The Rangarajan Expert Group (report 2014) built its poverty line on separate food and non-food needs.

new.s: In which year was the Tendulkar Expert Group on poverty estimation set up?
new.x: The Tendulkar Expert Group was set up in 2005 and gave its report in 2009.
new.angle: U0397 #1 Expert groups -> year set up

new.s: To whom is the MGNREGA guarantee of at least 100 days of wage work in a financial year given?
o: Each adult individual in rural areas
new.x: The 100-day guarantee is per rural household in a financial year, not per adult individual.

new.s: In which year was the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act passed by Parliament?
new.x: NREGA was passed in August 2005; it came into force on 2 February 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA in 2009.

new.s: Which type of unemployment is temporary and occurs while workers are changing or searching for jobs?
new.x: Frictional unemployment is short-term joblessness while people change or look for jobs; it is mainly urban.

new.s: In which sector is seasonal unemployment mainly found in India?
new.x: Seasonal unemployment means work only in some months of the year; it is mainly found in agriculture.

new.s: Denial of property, work and mobility to women is an example of social exclusion based on which of the following?
new.x: Denying women property, work and mobility is exclusion on the basis of gender.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an indicator of the standard-of-living dimension of the National MPI?
new.x: Cooking fuel, bank accounts and electricity are standard-of-living indicators; nutrition belongs to the health dimension.

new.s: Under PLFS, which status measures a person's activity over the reference year?
new.x: Usual status looks at activity over the reference year; CWS uses 7 days and CDS each day of the week.

new.s: What was the main aim of TRYSEM, launched in 1979 as a component of IRDP?
new.x: TRYSEM (Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment) trained rural youth and was a part of IRDP.

new.s:
Consider the following parts of the Indian Constitution:
1. Preamble
2. Directive Principles of State Policy
3. Fundamental Duties
In which of the above are the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights reflected?
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: UDHR ideals of justice, equality and liberty are reflected in the Preamble, the Directive Principles and the Fundamental Duties.
new.angle: U0398 PYQ y9d017f1eea7 Constitution part -> UDHR consonance

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Every Fundamental Right is a human right.
2. Every human right is a Fundamental Right in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Every Fundamental Right is a human right, but not every human right (for example, the right to vote, which is statutory) is a Fundamental Right.
new.angle: U0398 #4 Concept / PYQ yfa9a50f3ff7 Fundamental Rights vs human rights

new.s: What was the theme of Human Rights Day observed in December 2024?
o: Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now
Dignity, Freedom and Justice for All
Stand up for someone's rights today
Equality: Reducing inequalities, advancing human rights
new.x: Human Rights Day on 10 December 2024 had the theme 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now'.
new.angle: U0398 #3 / PYQ y965c64ebbc4 Human Rights Day -> theme

new.s: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Declaration on the Right to Development?
new.x: The right to development was recognised by a UNGA Declaration in 1986.

new.s: Which of the following entered into force first?
new.x: The ICESCR came into force on 3 January 1976, before the ICCPR (23 March 1976); CEDAW and CRC came later.

new.s: Where is the UN Human Rights Council based?
new.x: The Human Rights Council, set up in 2006, is based in Geneva.

new.s: What is the term of a member of the UN Human Rights Council?
new.x: Members of the 47-member Council are elected by the UNGA for 3-year terms, at most two in a row.

new.s: Which UN convention, ratified by India in 1968, deals with racial discrimination?
new.x: CERD (1965) deals with racial discrimination; India ratified it in 1968.
new.angle: U0398 #8 Core treaties -> subject and India's status

new.s:

1. Section 31 provides for a Special Public Prosecutor for every Human Rights Court.
2. The Special Public Prosecutor must be an advocate with at least seven years' practice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Section 31 lets the State Government specify a Special Public Prosecutor, an advocate of at least 7 years' practice, for each Human Rights Court.
new.angle: U0399 #4 Special Public Prosecutor -> Section and experience

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Article 21A, the right to education for children aged 6 to 14?
new.x: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making education for 6-14 year olds a Fundamental Right.
new.angle: U0399 #2 Fundamental and human rights -> Article 21A amendment

new.s: Who called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
new.x: Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies) the heart and soul of the Constitution.

new.s: In which case was the right to livelihood read into Article 21?
new.x: In Olga Tellis (1985), the pavement dwellers case, the Supreme Court held that the right to life includes the right to livelihood.

new.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the right to life under Article 21 includes the right to live with human dignity?
new.x: Francis Coralie Mullin (1981) read the right to live with human dignity into Article 21.

new.s: Which Directive Principle asks the State to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations?
new.x: Article 51(c), a Directive Principle, asks the State to respect international law; Article 253 is Parliament's power to implement treaties.

new.s: Below what age does Article 24 prohibit the employment of children in factories, mines and hazardous work?
new.x: Article 24 bars employing children below 14 years in factories, mines and hazardous work.

new.s: Which Articles together make up the Right against Exploitation?
new.x: The Right against Exploitation consists of Article 23 (traffic and forced labour) and Article 24 (child labour).

new.s: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission constituted?
new.x: The NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993; the Act only got assent in January 1994, so '1994' is a trap.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission:
1. It is a constitutional body.
2. It was constituted on 12 October 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The NHRC is a statutory body under the PHRA, 1993, not a constitutional one; it was constituted on 12 October 1993.

new.s: Who appoints the Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission?
new.x: The President appoints them on the advice of a six-member committee headed by the Prime Minister.

new.s: Who can be appointed Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission after the 2019 amendment?
o: Only a former Chief Justice of a High Court
A former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court
Only a former Judge of the Supreme Court
Any District Judge with seven years' service
new.x: Since 2019 a former High Court Judge, not only a former High Court Chief Justice, can chair an SHRC.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about a State Human Rights Commission:
1. In a vacancy in the office of Chairperson, the Governor may authorise a member to act as Chairperson.
2. The Chief Justice of the High Court is a member of the committee that selects its Chairperson.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Governor authorises an acting Chairperson; the High Court Chief Justice is only consulted for judge members and is not on the CM-led selection committee.
new.angle: U0400 #20 SHRC -> acting Chairperson and consultation

new.s: In which case did the Supreme Court lay down 16-point guidelines on encounter deaths in 2014?
o: D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal
Prakash Singh v Union of India
Nilabati Behera v State of Orissa
new.x: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) set 16-point guidelines on encounter deaths, used with NHRC reporting norms.
new.angle: U0400 #9 Specialised mandates -> encounter deaths guidelines

new.s: Who was the Chairperson of the Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission when its Kurnool office was inaugurated in 2021?
new.x: Justice M. Seetharama Murti, a retired High Court judge, was the AP SHRC Chairperson when the Kurnool office opened in September 2021.

new.s: According to Amnesty International, which country is the world's biggest executioner?
new.x: Amnesty International reports name China as the biggest executioner in the world.
new.angle: U0401 #2 Death penalty -> global execution ranking

new.s: In Shatrughan Chauhan v Union of India (2014), how many days' notice before execution was held necessary after a mercy petition is rejected?
new.x: Shatrughan Chauhan (2014) required 14 days between rejection of mercy and execution, and held delay a ground for commutation.
new.angle: U0401 #8 Mercy petitions -> Shatrughan Chauhan issues

new.s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, which State/UT had the highest prison occupancy rate?
new.x: Delhi's prisons were the most overcrowded at 194.6% occupancy, ahead of Meghalaya (163.5%); the national rate was 112.7%.

new.s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita provides the punishment for murder?
new.x: Murder is punishable under Section 103 of the BNS, which replaced Section 302 of the IPC.
new.angle: U0401 #2 Death penalty -> BNS section for murder

new.s: Which BNSS section requires sanction before a court takes cognisance of an offence against a public servant?
new.x: BNSS Section 218 requires prior sanction against public servants, which can delay prosecution in custodial cases.

new.s: Which of the following statements on women is attributed to B.R. Ambedkar?
o: A bird cannot fly on one wing
I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved
To call woman the weaker sex is a libel
You can tell the condition of a nation by looking at the status of its women
new.x: Ambedkar measured a community's progress by the progress of its women; the other lines are Vivekananda's, Gandhi's and Nehru's.

new.s: Who said, 'You can tell the condition of a nation by looking at the status of its women'?
new.x: This statement on the status of women is Jawaharlal Nehru's.

new.x: The bar on women aged 10-50 was struck down 4:1; Justice Indu Malhotra was the only woman judge on the bench and dissented.

new.s: Who were the first women of menstruating age to enter the Sabarimala temple after the 2018 verdict?

new.x: Bindu Ammini and Kanaka Durga entered in January 2019; Zakia Soman and Noorjehan Safia Niaz were the Haji Ali petitioners.
new.angle: U0402 #14 Women and religion -> persons involved

new.s: Who founded the All India Women's Conference in 1927?
new.x: Margaret Cousins founded the AIWC in 1927; she had also co-founded the Women's Indian Association in 1917 with Annie Besant.

new.s: Who founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873?
new.x: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873; with Savitribai he also started the first girls' school at Pune.

new.s: Which social reformer is associated with the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856?
new.x: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar campaigned for the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.

new.s: Which committee reviewed the laws on sexual violence in 2013, after the Nirbhaya case?
new.x: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee (2013) reviewed sexual violence laws, leading to the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.

new.s: With which journal is Madhu Kishwar associated?
new.x: Madhu Kishwar founded the women's journal Manushi in the post-1970s women's movement.

new.s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, which body handles complaints at the district level?
new.x: Workplaces with 10 or more employees have an Internal Complaints Committee; the Local Committee works at the district level.

new.s: Who chairs the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women (as of December 2025)?
new.x: Rayapati Sailaja chairs the AP Women's Commission, set up under the A.P. Women's Commission Act, 1998.
